And Peter {{ls}}aith to him, Lord, doe{{ls}}t thou vva{{ls}}h my feete? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=7}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered and {{ls}}aid to him, That vvhich I doe, thou knovve{{ls}}t not novv, hereafter thou {{ls}}halt knovv. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=8}} Peter {{ls}}aith to him, Thou {{ls}}halt not wa{{ls}}h my feete for euer. {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered him, If I vva{{ls}}h thee not, thou {{ls}}halt not haue part vvith me. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=9}} Simon Peter {{ls}}aith to him, Lord, not only my feete, but al{{ls}}o handes, and head. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=10}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to him, He that is vva{{ls}}hed, nedeeth not but {{sup|‖}} to wa{{ls}}h his feete, but is cleane vvholy. And you are cleane, but not al. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=11}} For he knevv vvho he vvas that vvould betray him. therfore he {{ls}}aid, You are not cleane al.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=12}} Therfore, after he had vva{{ls}}hed their feete, and taken his garments, being {{ls}}et dovvne, againe he {{ls}}aid to them, Knovv you what I haue done to you? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=13}} You cal me, Mai{{ls}}ter, and Lord: and you {{ls}}ay vvel, for I am {{ls}}o. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=14}} If then I haue wa{{ls}}hed your feete, Lord and Mai{{ls}}ter, {{sup|‖}} you al{{ls}}o ought to wa{{ls}}h one an others feete. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=15}} For I haue giuen you an example, that as I haue done to you, {{ls}}o you doe al{{ls}}o.⊣ {{verse|chapter=13|verse=16}} Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, a {{ls}}eruant is not greater then his lord, neither is an apo{{ls}}tle greater then he that {{ls}}ent him. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=17}} If you know the{{ls}}e things, you {{ls}}hal be ble{{ls}}{{ls}}ed if you doe them. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=18}} I {{ls}}peake not of you al: I knovv vvhom I haue cho{{ls}}en. But that the {{ls}}cripture may be fulfilled, ''He that eateth bread vvith me, {{ls}}hal lift vp his heele again{{ls}}t me''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''P{{ls}}. 40, 10.''}} {{verse|chapter=13|verse=19}} From this time I tel you, before it come to pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e: that vvhen it {{ls}}hal come to pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e, you may beleeue, that I am he. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=20}} Amen, amen, I {{ls}}ay to you, he that receiueth any that I {{ls}}end, receiueth me: & he that receiueth me, receiueth him that {{ls}}ent me.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=21}} When {{sc|Iesvs}} had {{ls}}aid the{{ls}}e things, he vvas troubled in {{ls}}pirit: and he prote{{ls}}ted, and {{ls}}aid: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 26, 18. Mar. 14, 16. Luc. 22, 21.''}}* Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you: that one of you {{ls}}hal betray me. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=22}} The di{{ls}}ciples therfore looked one vpon an other, doubting of whom he {{ls}}pake. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=23}} There vvas therfore one of his di{{ls}}ciples leaning in the bo{{ls}}ome of {{sc|Iesvs}}, he whom {{sc|Iesvs}} loued. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=24}} Therfore Simon Peter beckeneth to him, and {{ls}}aid to him, who is it of whom he {{ls}}peaketh? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=25}} He therfore leaning vpon the brea{{ls}}t of {{sc|Iesvs}}, {{ls}}aith to him, Lord, vvho is he? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=26}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered: He it is<noinclude>{{continues|to}}</noinclude>
